raw_case_text:
A 10-year-old girl was admitted to our hospital on May 3, 2022, due to fever and cough for 3 days; respiratory symptoms worsened and dyspnea developed 1 day prior to admission. Fever was present during this period, and body temperature fluctuating between 37.4 C and 38.3 C. Her respiratory symptoms were characterized by dry cough and progressive dyspnea. She was treated with antibiotics in another hospital, but the symptoms did not improve. Therefore, she was transferred to our department.
She was diagnosed with idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) in November 2021 at an another hospital. She was initiated on oral prednisone at a dose of 2 mg/kg/day, which was gradually tapered. At the time of admission to our hospital, she was receiving prednisone 15 mg twice daily.
On admission, the girl was alert, communicative, tachypneic (RR 50/min) with fine basal rales on chest auscultation; and no special conditions in other important organs and systems.
Laboratory examination: white blood cell count (WBC) 5.85 x 109/L, neutrophil (NE) 4.92 x 109/L, hemoglobin (HGB) 108 g/L, platelets (PLT) 261 x 109/L, C-reactive protein (CRP) 25.2 mg/L (reference range 0-3), procalcitonin (PCT) 0.27 ng/ml (reference range 0-0.05), plasma (1,3)-beta- D-glucan test (BDG) 154.2 pg/ml (reference range 0-60), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 1495 U/L (reference range 120-246), serum ferritin level 282.6 ng/ml(reference range 4-204). Gram-negative bacteria lipopolysaccharide was negative. Serology assays for HIV, CMV, HCV, and HBV were negative. Liver and renal function, electrolytes, and myocardial enzymes were normal. The serum levels of immunoglobulin M, G, and A were normal. The CD4+ lymphocyte count, B lymphocyte count and NK cell count were normal. Blood gas analysis: PH 7.39,pCO2 26 mmHg,pO2 50 mmHg,Lac 0.7 mmol/L,BE -8 mmol/L,SaO2 88.7%. Chest X-ray indicated diffuse exudative lesion in both lungs (Figure 1).
After admission, she was intubated and mechanically ventilated. Meropenem was used for anti-infective treatment. On the third day after hospitalization, metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of blood detected Pneumocystis jirovecii with a specific sequence number of 326 (Figure 2A). mNGS of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) also detected Pneumocystis jirovecii with the specific sequence number of 2644 (Figure 2B), and the antibiotics were adjusted to caspofungin combined with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMZ). 6 days after admission, the blood and BALF bacterial culture was negative. The girl was treated with prone position ventilation, due to pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (pARDS) was considered. Despite above treatments, the child's respiratory condition did not improve. On the 10th day, her body temperature fluctuated between 38 C and 40 C, laboratory examination showed that WBC, NE, HGB and PLT decreased to 0.65 x 109/L, 0.14 x 109/L, 62 g/L, 51 x 109/L, respectively; serum ferritin level was increased progressively at 1351.76 ng/ml; fibrinogen (FIB) was reduced to 1 g/L; triglycerides increased to 3.85 mmol/L; an NK cell activity assay was 2% (reference range >= 4%); solubleinter leukin-2 receptor levels (sCD25) was 2421 U/ml (reference range 223-710) (Figure 3). Due to the laboratory testing limitations of our hospital (the hospital's clinical laboratory does not have the corresponding detection kits and technical platforms for these two biomarkers), IL-18 and CD163 were not tested. Chest computed tomography (CT) showed extensive ground-glass opacities (GGO) in both lungs (Figure 4). Bone marrow aspirate showed an extensive hemophagocytosis (Figure 5). So she was diagnosed with HLH, but her parents refused to complete genetic investigations. Given the severity of the pulmonary infection, she was treated with dexamethasone in combination with continuous renal replacement treatment (CRRT) and plasmapheresis instead of chemotherapy. Unfortunately, her pulmonary infection was getting worse (Ventilator parameters: FIO2 100%, PEEP 12cmH2O, VT 6 ml/kg), and she was discharged on day 22, because her parents gave up treatment. We knew that she died on the day of discharge, through telephone follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 10-year-old girl on oral prednisone for idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura presented with a 3-day history of fever and dry cough and a 1-day history of rapidly worsening dyspnea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed fever (fluctuating between 37.4 °C and 38.3 °C) and a dry cough 3 days prior to admission on May 3, 2022, which progressed to severe dyspnea 1 day prior to admission despite empiric antibiotic treatment at an outside hospital. Six months earlier (November 2021), she had been diagnosed with idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) and started on oral prednisone (initially 2 mg/kg/day, maintained at 15 mg twice daily at the time of admission).
subjective.past_medical_history: Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) diagnosed in November 2021, treated with continuous oral prednisone for 6 months.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever (37.4–38.3 °C), dry cough, and progressive dyspnea. Home medication was oral prednisone 15 mg twice daily.

objective.physical_examination: On admission: Alert and communicative, marked tachypnea with respiratory rate 50 breaths/min, and fine basilar rales on chest auscultation; remainder of systemic exam unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission arterial blood gas: pH 7.39, pCO2 26 mmHg, pO2 50 mmHg, lactate 0.7 mmol/L, base excess -8 mmol/L, and SaO2 88.7%. Admission laboratory tests: WBC 5.85 x 10^9/L, neutrophils 4.92 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin 108 g/L, platelets 261 x 10^9/L, C-reactive protein (CRP) 25.2 mg/L (reference: 0–3 mg/L), procalcitonin (PCT) 0.27 ng/mL (reference: 0–0.05 ng/mL), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 1,495 U/L (reference: 120–246 U/L), and serum ferritin 282.6 ng/mL (reference: 4–204 ng/mL). Negative/normal baseline studies: Negative Gram-negative lipopolysaccharide, negative HIV, CMV, HBV, and HCV serologies, negative blood and BALF bacterial cultures (day 6), and normal hepatic/renal function, electrolytes, myocardial enzymes, and serum IgG, IgA, and IgM. Admission chest X-ray: Diffuse bilateral exudative pulmonary lesions. Day 10 HLH progression labs: Pancytopenia with WBC 0.65 x 10^9/L, neutrophils 0.14 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin 62 g/L, and platelets 51 x 10^9/L; serum ferritin surged to 1,351.76 ng/mL; fibrinogen decreased to 1 g/L; triglycerides rose to 3.85 mmol/L.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission fungal biomarker and lymphocyte subsets: Elevated plasma (1,3)-beta-D-glucan (BDG) at 154.2 pg/mL (reference: 0–60 pg/mL); normal baseline CD4+ T-cell, B-cell, and NK-cell counts. Day 3 metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS): Peripheral blood mNGS detected 326 specific sequence reads of Pneumocystis jirovecii, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) mNGS detected 2,644 specific sequence reads of Pneumocystis jirovecii. Day 10 secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) workup: Chest CT showed extensive bilateral ground-glass opacities (GGOs); NK-cell activity decreased to 2% (reference >=4%); soluble IL-2 receptor (sCD25) elevated to 2,421 U/mL (reference: 223–710 U/mL); bone marrow aspirate demonstrated extensive hemophagocytosis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Severe Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP; confirmed by 2,644 reads on BALF mNGS, 326 reads on blood mNGS, plasma BDG 154.2 pg/mL, and LDH 1,495 U/L) complicated by pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (pARDS) and secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH; confirmed by bone marrow hemophagocytosis, pancytopenia, ferritin 1,351.76 ng/mL, hypofibrinogenemia 1 g/L, hypertriglyceridemia 3.85 mmol/L, NK activity 2%, and sCD25 2,421 U/mL) in a 10-year-old girl on chronic corticosteroids for ITP. Plan and clinical course: Immediately intubated for invasive mechanical ventilation (with prone positioning) and started on empiric meropenem, which was switched on day 3 after mNGS confirmation to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) plus caspofungin. When she developed high fevers (38–40 °C) and secondary HLH on day 10, she was treated with intravenous dexamethasone, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), and plasmapheresis. Despite maximal ventilatory support (FiO2 100%, PEEP 12 cmH2O), her respiratory failure worsened; her parents elected to withdraw care on day 22, and she died on the day of discharge.
